routing.reason: Tags span a new migration, the API (create, patch, list filter, /api/tags), the one-page UI and tests/README, in a small codebase (~370 lines) with fully testable acceptance criteria.
rulings: Ruling: default workflow, not direct — the work is M, crosses back (API, migration) and front (page) and the ticket asks for a new table, so one task is not enough — cost if wrong: a slightly heavier run than needed.
Ruling: skip the product owner (frame) — the ticket already lists 8 testable acceptance criteria — cost if wrong: a missed edge case, caught by the code review.

Ruling: no PM, no architect, no UX, no SEO — the design is given (separate tags and task_tags tables, existing page patterns, no public pages) — cost if wrong: the plan lead has to decide the page's tag-filter layout itself.

Ruling: security review at medium effort — tags are user input parsed and bound into SQL filters, but there is no authentication, payment or personal data — cost if wrong: a missed injection or validation gap, mitigated by prepared statements and the HTML escaping check on the page.

Ruling: the DBA migration review stays on (default) — a new migration adds tables with foreign keys; it must be a new entry in `src/db.ts` with ON DELETE CASCADE, never an edit of the shipped one (foreign_keys is already ON) — cost if wrong: orphaned links on task deletion.

Ruling: note for the plan — the current `done` filter in `src/tasks.ts` treats the string "false" as truthy, so `?done=false` returns done tasks; since AC4 requires the tag filter to combine with `done`, the plan must fix and test it as part of this work — cost if wrong: the combined filter returns wrong results.

Ruling: note for the plan — invalid-tag requests must answer 400 `{"error":"invalid tags"}` before any write (validate, then write in one transaction), and a non-array `tags` is invalid too; page tag rendering must escape tag text (no innerHTML with raw values) — cost if wrong: partial writes or XSS on the page.

Ruling: budget $2.00 — covers the plan, back and front tasks, a QA task, the review rounds, the DBA review and the security review for an M change — cost if wrong: the run stops before its reviews and the user must raise it.

criteria.why: withTags always sets tags from links ordered by t.name, defaulting to []; tested.
POST and PATCH parse tags; PATCH replaces via setTags only when defined; tests cover replace, keep and clear.
normalizeTags trims, lowercases, dedups, checks the pattern and max 10 after dedup, and the route returns 400 'invalid tags'. Validation runs before any write, and many invalid cases are tested.
The tag filter is normalized and combined with done through an EXISTS clause; tests cover combinations.
listTags joins task_tags, groups and sorts by name, so unused tags are dropped; tested.
New migration adds tags and task_tags with ON DELETE CASCADE; a test checks links are removed and the upgrade from v1.
The page renders tag buttons, filters on click, has an 'All tags' reset and a comma-separated tags input.
API tests are added and the README documents the tags endpoints and rules.

findings.what: Adds a new 400 'invalid done' for GET /api/tasks?done=other. Previously any other value was treated as open. This is an unrequested behavior change and could break existing clients. It also changed the listTasks signature from string to boolean.
Adds a test for ?done=false/true and for the invalid done value, which are outside the ticket.

A null or non-object JSON body (e.g. `null`) makes body.tags throw, and malformed JSON throws in readJson. The diff adds new uses of body.tags without guarding, so such requests are likely to produce a 500 or a crash. This is pre-existing but extended.
withTags loads every task_tags link in the database for every call, even when returning a single task. This is O(total links) per request; it should filter by task ids.
Tags that are no longer used stay in the tags table forever (never cleaned up). Listing is correct, but rows accumulate.
The ?tag test has a stray `assert.equal(a.status, 201)` and an unused variable. The 'ids' helper actually returns titles.

The tag filter sets currentTag, but the form submit does not report an invalid tag in a friendly way beyond showing the server message. Tags typed in the add form are not lowercased client side, which is fine because the server normalizes.

judge.summary: The diff meets every acceptance criterion with a clean migration, transactional writes, validation before any change, and thorough API tests including a migration upgrade test. Points off for the unrequested `done` validation that changes existing behavior, no guard against null JSON bodies, and loading every tag link on each query.
